p: Ilkley is easy to get to without a car, which is a bonus for a family day out. Trains run up the Wharfedale line from Leeds and Bradford, and the station is right in the town centre, close to the cafes and shops.

Before you climb, everyone will need a participation form, with a parent or guardian signing for under-18s. Doing it online saves time at the desk. Check the age guidance when you book, as there's usually a minimum age for climbers and supervision rules for little ones. Give yourselves a couple of hours for the full visit.
A tip for the walls: use your legs. Pushing up through your feet saves your arms, and you'll manage far more challenges before the burn sets in.

Afterwards, the Manor House, on the site of the old Roman fort near the church, has displays on Ilkley's long history. In summer, the open-air Ilkley Lido is a much-loved spot for a dip. And if you've got a car and a bit more time, Bolton Abbey is a short drive up the valley, with its priory ruins, riverside paths and the famous stepping stones across the Wharfe. Otley, just down the river, is another characterful market town for a wander and a bite to eat.
